CA.injury: In California you generally have two years from the accident to file a lawsuit (Code of Civil Procedure §335.1) — and if a city, county, or state agency is involved (a bus, a public road, a government vehicle) you may have as little as six months to file a claim. Evidence disappears far sooner: camera footage gets erased and witnesses move. The sooner we start, the stronger your case.
CA.employment: Deadlines are shorter than people think. Discrimination, harassment, and retaliation claims under California's Fair Employment and Housing Act must be filed with the Civil Rights Department within three years. Wrongful termination in violation of public policy generally carries a two-year deadline. Unpaid-wage claims reach back three years (up to four under the Unfair Competition Law). Some notice deadlines are far shorter — so get a free review now, not after the deadline passes.

NV.injury: In Nevada you generally have two years from the accident to file a lawsuit (NRS 11.190) — and claims involving a government vehicle or public property carry their own notice rules. Evidence disappears far sooner: camera footage gets erased and witnesses move. The sooner we start, the stronger your case.
NV.employment: Nevada and federal discrimination claims generally must be filed with the Nevada Equal Rights Commission or the EEOC within 300 days. Wage claims carry their own deadlines. Don't wait — get a free review now.
